parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define gravitational field at a point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Fig. 3.1 shows an isolated point mass of mass *M*.

[[fig:f1]]

Point P is at distance *x* from the point mass.
parts.text: By considering the force exerted by the point mass on a test mass of mass *m* placed at P, derive an equation for the gravitational field strength *g* at P, in terms of *M* and *x*. Identify any other symbols you use.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: On Fig. 3.1, draw an arrow to indicate the direction of the gravitational field at P.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Point Q is at distance $\frac{x}{2}$ from the point mass on the opposite side of the mass from P, as shown in Fig. 3.2.

[[fig:f2]]

Compare the gravitational field at Q with that at P.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Two identical isolated uniform spheres X and Y each have radius *R*. The centres of the spheres are separated by distance *L*, as shown in Fig. 3.3.

[[fig:f3]]

Point P lies on the line joining the centres of X and Y, and is at a variable displacement *x* from the centre of sphere X.
The gravitational field strength at the surface of each sphere is *g*₀.

On Fig. 3.4, sketch the variation with *x* of the gravitational field *g* at point P between *x* = *R* and *x* = *L* − *R*.

[[fig:f4]]

figures.caption: Fig. 3.1
figures.alt: A point mass of mass M and point P are separated by distance x.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.2
figures.alt: Point Q lies x/2 to the left of mass M and point P lies x to its right.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.3
figures.alt: Spheres X and Y are separated by distance L, with point P at distance x from the centre of X.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.4
figures.alt: A gridded graph for gravitational field g against displacement x, with marked values from −g₀ to g₀ and positions R, L/2 and L−R.
